docs.title: Ponvara
docs.text:
A finding bus: pulls security findings from sources that cannot push to DefectDojo themselves and reimports them. Runs as a CronJob; will be generalized to a long-lived scheduler with zero-touch GitHub-issue push for High and Critical findings (future).

It promotes an existing, working-but-fragile in-cluster CronJob (dt-defectdojo-sync) into a tested, versioned service, and generalises it so a new source is a new connector module rather than a new CronJob.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Dependency-Track ─┐
 GitHub Adv. Sec. ─┤                    ┌─→ DefectDojo (reimport-scan, dedupe, SLA)
 SonarQube ────────┤──▶  Ponvara ───────┤
 DAST (ZAP/Nuclei)─┤     (connectors)   └─→ GitHub Issues (zero-touch, High/Crit — future)
 <future source> ──┘
  • Sources: Dependency-Track, GitHub Advanced Security, and future connectors pull findings.
  • Sink: DefectDojo (via reimport-scan). GitHub Issues push is Phase 2 work.
  • Current phase: CLI with ponvara sync and ponvara sync-github commands (CronJob-based). Each command runs once and exits, scheduled via Kubernetes CronJob and Helm chart.
  • Future phases: long-lived Deployment with APScheduler, on-demand endpoints, GitHub-issue push.

docs.title: Why the REST API, not the Django ORM
docs.text:
The legacy job reaches into DefectDojo's private Django data model for two things. The first has been replaced; the second is future work:

Django ORM usage REST replacement Status Mint a superuser API token via Token.objects.get_or_create Provision one DefectDojo API token for a dedicated ponvara service user, once, stored in OCI Vault. No ORM, no password. ✅ Done (Phase 1) Finding.objects.filter(...) + GITHUB_Issue.objects.create(...) for GitHub-issue dedupe GET /api/v2/findings/ (filter by product/severity/active); dedupe by writing a finding tag gh-issue:<url> via PATCH /api/v2/findings/{id}/. State lives in DefectDojo, service stays stateless. 📋 Phase 2 (GitHub-issue push feature)

Result: Ponvara runs on a slim python:3.12-slim image (~80 MB) and is fully decoupled from DefectDojo's version — DefectDojo chart upgrades no longer force a lockstep bump. This removes the biggest fragility of the current setup.

docs.title: How it fits the security programme
docs.text:
Ponvara is the runtime / continuous half of the security tooling estate; it complements the others rather than overlapping them:

  • MagmaMoose/chargate — the PR-time SAST/SCA/IaC gate (a MegaLinter wrapper with net-new gating). Chargate acts before merge on a single PR; Ponvara acts continuously on deployed/portfolio-wide findings. Chargate already ships full SARIF to DefectDojo and BOMs to Dependency-Track; Ponvara moves what those tools produce onward.
  • MagmaMoose/draventis — scheduled DAST (ZAP + Nuclei) → DefectDojo. ZAP/Nuclei have native DefectDojo parsers, so draventis pushes straight to DefectDojo; if a bespoke DAST result shape ever needs orchestration/enrichment, it becomes a Ponvara connector.
  • MagmaMoose/security-platform — the program index and security-tooling roadmap that ties chargate, draventis, Ponvara, DefectDojo, and Dependency-Track together.
  • DefectDojo (self-hosted, private infra repo) — the aggregation/dedupe/SLA system of record. Ponvara is its feeder for sources that can't push themselves.
  • Dependency-Track (self-hosted, private infra repo) — the SBOM/SCA source. Dependency-Track has no "push to DefectDojo"; Ponvara pulls its FPF export and reimports it. This is the original job the bus was born from.

docs.text:
• Design — the full design document
  • Roadmap — what is built, what is next, what is undecided

docs.title: Ponvara — Design
docs.text:
Status: Phase 1 complete (REST API slim image with Dependency-Track and GHAS syncs) · Date: 2026-08-27

Promote the in-cluster dt-defectdojo-sync CronJob (and its SonarQube sibling) into its own repo, container, and Helm chart — a long-lived, tested, versioned backend deployed separately via Flux — and generalize it into a finding bus. Scope is deliberately bounded: this does not widen chargate's PR-time gate; Ponvara is the continuous/runtime counterpart.

docs.title: 1. What exists today
docs.text:
In the private infra repo (kubernetes/apps/security-integrations/):

Resource What it does configmap-sync-script.yaml ~180-line sync.py embedded in YAML cronjob-dt-sync.yaml Hourly CronJob; runs sync.py inside defectdojo/defectdojo-django:2.58.4 cronjob-sonarqube-sync.yaml Sibling, +30m offset, own embedded script configmap-sonarqube-sync.yaml The SonarQube script externalsecret-sync.yaml DTRACK_API_KEY, SONARQUBE_TOKEN from OCI Vault externalsecret-github-targets.yaml GITHUB_TARGETS JSON (server + owners + PAT) from OCI Vault

sync.py does two jobs per Dependency-Track project:

  1. Export findings as FPF → DefectDojo reimport-scan (auto_create_context, close_old_findings, dedupe). One DefectDojo product per Dependency-Track project.
  2. Zero-touch GitHub issue auto-push: resolve a repo by matching the Dependency-Track project name to <owner>/<name> across configured GitHub accounts (github.com first, then GHE), open issues for new High/Critical Active findings, and record a GITHUB_Issue so re-runs dedupe.

The critical coupling: it runs inside the DefectDojo Django image and uses the Django ORM for exactly two things — (a) minting a superuser API token without a password (Token.objects.get_or_create), and (b) the GitHub-issue dedupe/query (Finding.objects.filter(...), GITHUB_Issue.objects.create(...)).

docs.title: 2. Why promote it (the problems)
docs.text:
• Code-in-YAML. No tests, no linting, no type-checking, no CI, painful review and diffs. A security-critical integration deserves the same rigor as chargate.
  • Image coupling + version lockstep. Pinned to defectdojo-django:2.58.4 so the ORM matches the live DB schema — every DefectDojo chart upgrade forces a lockstep bump, and the image is ~1 GB. This is the single biggest fragility.
  • ORM coupling to DefectDojo internals. Importing dojo.models / dojo.github.models ties the job to DefectDojo's private data model across versions.
  • Mixed concerns, no reuse. DT sync, SonarQube sync, and GitHub push are three copies/variants with no shared library, no versioning, no release artifact.
  • Batch-only. CronJobs can't be triggered on demand, expose no health/metrics, and there's nowhere to add a webhook (e.g. "DT analysis finished → sync now").

The goal is a long-lived backend, in a repo, with a Helm chart, deployed separately. That's the right call — and it unlocks a bigger idea below.

docs.title: 3. The bigger framing: a finding bus, not just a DT sync
docs.text:
Once it's a real service, generalize it slightly. It becomes the orchestration + enrichment layer that sits beside DefectDojo:

 Dependency-Track ─┐
 SonarQube ────────┤                         ┌─→ DefectDojo (reimport-scan, dedupe, SLA)
 DAST (ZAP/Nuclei)─┤──▶  Ponvara  ────┤
 <future source> ──┘     (connectors +       └─→ GitHub Issues (zero-touch, High/Crit)
                          scheduler + API)

Not everything needs this bus — Trivy Operator, Prowler, ZAP, Nuclei have native DefectDojo parsers (see the security-tooling roadmap), so those push straight to DefectDojo. Scheduled DAST is owned by draventis, which uses those native parsers. The bus earns its keep for exactly the cases the current CronJob handles:

  • Movement DefectDojo can't do itself — Dependency-Track has no "push to DefectDojo"; something must pull FPF and reimport. Same for any source lacking a native DefectDojo path.
  • Cross-cutting enrichment — the zero-touch GitHub-issue auto-push (repo resolution by name across owners) is logic DefectDojo's per-product GitHub config can't do generically. This is the real value-add and belongs in one place.

So: keep it focused (DT + SonarQube + GitHub-issue push at launch), but structure it so a new source is a new connector module.

docs.title: 4. Target architecture
docs.text:
Language: Python 3.11+ (the runtime image targets 3.12-slim), packaged with uv + Ruff + pytest + full type hints — mirror chargate's conventions exactly (and its broker/ deploy pattern).

The one design decision that unlocks everything: drop the Django ORM, use the DefectDojo REST API v2. Replace the two ORM usages:

ORM usage today REST replacement Mint superuser token via Token.objects Provision one DefectDojo API token (a dedicated ponvara service user) once, store in OCI Vault. No ORM, no password. Finding.objects.filter(...) + GITHUB_Issue.objects.create(...) for dedupe Query GET /api/v2/findings/ (filter by product/severity/active); dedupe by writing a finding tag gh-issue:<url> (or a note) via PATCH /api/v2/findings/{id}/. State lives in DefectDojo, so the service stays stateless.

Result: run on a slim python:3.12-slim image (~80 MB), fully decoupled from DefectDojo's version. This alone removes the worst fragility.

docs.title: Repo layout
docs.text:
ponvara/
  pyproject.toml                # uv; deps: httpx, pydantic-settings, apscheduler,
                                #   fastapi+uvicorn, PyGithub (or raw httpx), prometheus-client
  src/ponvara/
    config.py                   # pydantic-settings: sources, schedules, thresholds, secret refs
    defectdojo.py               # REST client: reimport-scan (SINK) [Phase 1]
    dependencytrack.py          # REST client: list projects, export FPF (SOURCE) [Phase 1]
    github.py                   # REST client: pull GHAS findings (SOURCE) [Phase 1]
    sync.py                     # orchestrator: DT → DefectDojo [Phase 1]
    sync_github.py              # orchestrator: GHAS → DefectDojo [Phase 1]
    # Future files (Phase 2+):
    app.py                      # FastAPI: /healthz /readyz /metrics + POST /sync/{source}
    scheduler.py                # APScheduler: interval jobs per enabled source
    github_issues.py            # zero-touch repo resolve + issue push (SINK) [Phase 2]
    sonarqube.py                # REST client: pull findings (SOURCE) [Phase 4]
    models.py                   # typed Finding/Project DTOs
  charts/ponvara/        # Helm chart (below)
  tests/                        # mirror modules 1:1 (pure connectors, injected HTTP)
  Dockerfile                    # slim, non-root, distroless-ish
  .github/workflows/            # ci.yml (ruff+pytest), release.yml (semantic-release + GHCR image)

Phase 1 status. Complete. The repo contains the connector modules (Dependency-Track, GitHub Advanced Security, DefectDojo), full test coverage (pure connectors, HTTP-mocked), configuration management, CLI (sync + sync-github commands), and the Helm chart (CronJob deployments). Dockerfile and GitHub Actions workflows are in place. Phase 2+ work (GitHub-issue push, long-lived service, generalization) remains future.

docs.title: Runtime shape — long-lived Deployment
docs.text:
A single Deployment (replicas: 1, Recreate) running uvicorn:

  • In-process scheduler (APScheduler) runs each source on its interval — replaces the two CronJobs, keeps offsets, adds jitter.
  • HTTP surface: /healthz, /readyz, /metrics (Prometheus), and POST /sync/{source} for on-demand runs (handy for testing + future DT webhooks).
  • concurrency: Forbid semantics via an in-process lock per source.
  • Emits metrics: ponvara_sync_findings_total{source}, ..._github_issues_total, ..._last_success_timestamp{source}, ..._errors_total.

Simpler alternative if a daemon isn't wanted: keep CronJobs but from our own slim image (chart kind: CronJob). You still get the repo/tests/CI/decoupling wins; you lose on-demand triggers + metrics. The Helm chart can support both via a mode: deployment|cronjob value. Recommendation: Deployment — it's literally the "long-lived backend" described here, and the incremental ops cost is tiny.

docs.title: Helm chart (charts/ponvara/)
docs.text:
values.yaml sketch (the full stub lives in charts/ponvara/values.yaml):

image: { repository: ghcr.io/magmamoose/ponvara, tag: "" }  # Flux ImagePolicy fills tag
mode: deployment                 # or "cronjob"
schedule: { dependencyTrack: "0 * * * *", sonarqube: "30 * * * *" }  # cron OR interval secs
defectDojo:
  url: http://defectdojo-django.security.svc.cluster.local
  productType: Dependency-Track
sources:
  dependencyTrack:
    enabled: true
    url: http://dependency-track-api-server.security.svc.cluster.local:8080
  sonarqube: { enabled: true, url: https://sonarqube.magmamoose.com }
github: { minSeverity: High, maxIssuesPerRun: 50 }
externalSecrets:                 # ESO -> OCI Vault (unchanged keys)
  store: oci-vault
  keys: { dtrackApiKey: dependency-track-api-key, ddApiToken: ponvara-dd-token,
          githubTargets: github-issue-targets, sonarToken: defectdojo-api-key }
resources: { requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 128Mi }, limits: { memory: 256Mi } }
serviceMonitor: { enabled: true }
ingress: { enabled: false }      # cloudflared tunnel if the trigger API is exposed
podSecurityContext: { runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 10001, seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault } }

Templates: deployment.yaml or cronjob.yaml (by mode), service.yaml, servicemonitor.yaml, externalsecret.yaml, serviceaccount.yaml (automountServiceAccountToken: false — it never calls the k8s API), _helpers.tpl. Ship the same hardening the SonarQube CronJob already uses (non-root high UID, RO rootfs, seccomp RuntimeDefault, no SA token).

docs.title: Deploy via Flux (mirror chargate/broker)
docs.text:
• infra/kubernetes/apps/ponvara/{base,prod}/ with a HelmRelease pointing at the chart (or a Flux Kustomization if the chart is vendored), an ImagePolicy autobumping the tag on each GHCR release, and the ExternalSecrets (reuse the existing OCI Vault keys; add one new key: ponvara-dd-token).
  • Retire kubernetes/apps/security-integrations/ once cut over.

docs.title: Image + release (mirror chargate)
docs.text: GHCR image ghcr.io/magmamoose/ponvara, built by a release.yml that runs python-semantic-release (version-from-commits) and a multi-arch docker buildx push — the exact pattern chargate already uses for its broker image. Flux's ImagePolicy rewrites the chart tag on publish. External GitHub Actions are SHA-pinned with a # vX.Y.Z comment.

docs.title: 5. Migration plan (low-risk, phased)
docs.text:
Phase Change Status Risk Reversible? 0. Lift-and-shift New repo; move sync.py verbatim; add tests around the pure bits (target parsing, severity floor, issue body). Still the DefectDojo-image CronJob, still deployed from infra. ✅ DONE none trivially 1. Slim the image Provision a ponvara DefectDojo API token (OCI Vault); replace ORM token-mint with it; switch to python:3.12-slim. Add GitHub Advanced Security sync (GHAS code scanning, Dependabot, secret scanning). ✅ DONE low keep old CronJob until green 2. GitHub-issue push + tag-based dedupe Implement zero-touch GitHub-issue push for High/Critical findings (requires DefectDojo findings query + tag-based state in DefectDojo). Now fully version-decoupled from DefectDojo. 📋 TODO med (verify tag/note dedupe survives reimport) run both in parallel one cycle 3. Long-lived service Convert to the FastAPI+APScheduler Deployment; add /metrics, /sync/{source}, ServiceMonitor; Helm chart; Flux app dir. Retire the infra CronJobs/ConfigMaps. 📋 TODO med Flux rollback 4. Generalize Fold SonarQube in as a connector; document how a new source plugs in. Point future non-native sources (e.g. a bespoke DAST result shape) here; leave native-parser tools (Trivy Operator, Prowler, ZAP, Nuclei) pushing straight to DefectDojo. 📋 TODO low per-connector toggle

You can stop after Phase 1 or 2 and already have a tested, reviewable, slim, version-decoupled job — most of the value is there. Phases 3–4 deliver the "long-lived backend" and the reuse.

docs.title: 6. Open decisions
docs.text:
1. Name. ponvara (descriptive) — chosen, matching the sibling repos draventis and security-platform under the MagmaMoose org. ✅ Resolved.
  2. REST API (Phase 1 decision) — chosen yes. Enables slim image, version-decoupled from DefectDojo. Phase 1 confirmed this works. ✅ Resolved.
  3. Tag/note-based dedupe for GitHub-issue push (Phase 2) — recommended yes. Must validate that reimport-scan preserves finding tags (if reimport recreates findings, fall back to stable finding hash instead).
  4. Deployment vs CronJob-from-own-image (Phase 3) — "long-lived backend" → Deployment. The chart supports both, so this is reversible.
  5. Dedup state for phase 2+: Stateless via DefectDojo tags (recommended) vs a tiny CNPG Postgres the service owns (needed only if cross-source correlation/SLA is tracked here later).

docs.title: 7. First PR (crawl)
docs.text: Create MagmaMoose/ponvara (this repo), uv init, drop sync.py in as src/ponvara/sync.py, split the GitHub-target parsing + severity-floor logic into pure functions, add tests/ for them, wire ci.yml (ruff + pytest). Keep the existing infra CronJob running untouched. That's Phase 0 — zero production risk, and it gives every later phase a tested base to refactor against.

docs.title: Related work
docs.text:
• MagmaMoose/chargate — PR-time SAST/SCA/IaC gate (MegaLinter wrapper with net-new gating). Ponvara mirrors its conventions and broker/ deploy pattern, and is the continuous/runtime counterpart to chargate's pre-merge gate.
  • MagmaMoose/draventis — scheduled DAST (ZAP + Nuclei) → DefectDojo via native parsers.
  • MagmaMoose/security-platform — the program index and security-tooling roadmap.
  • DefectDojo and Dependency-Track — self-hosted in the private infra repo; DefectDojo is the system of record, Dependency-Track the SBOM/SCA source this bus was born to feed.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text: Set up a development environment to run tests and build Ponvara from source.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or later
  • Git
  • uv (package and environment manager) — install from astral.sh/uv

docs.title: Clone and install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/MagmaMoose/ponvara
cd ponvara
uv sync

This creates a virtual environment and installs all dependencies (both runtime and development).

docs.title: Run tests
docs.text:
uv run pytest

Tests mock all HTTP clients, so no external services are required. The test suite covers:

  • Configuration loading
  • Dependency-Track and DefectDojo client behavior
  • GitHub Advanced Security client behavior
  • End-to-end sync logic

docs.title: Linting and type checking
docs.text:
The project uses Ruff for linting and formatting:

uv run ruff check src tests          # lint
uv run ruff format src tests         # auto-format

All code must pass linting before PR.

docs.title: Building the Docker image
docs.text:
docker build -t ponvara:dev .
docker run \
  -e DTRACK_API_URL=https://dtrack.example.com \
  -e DTRACK_API_KEY=<key> \
  -e DEFECTDOJO_URL=https://defectdojo.example.com \
  -e DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN=<token> \
  ponvara:dev ponvara sync

The Dockerfile builds on python:3.12-slim (~80 MB) and installs dependencies with uv.

docs.title: Running against live services
docs.text:
To test against actual Dependency-Track and DefectDojo instances:

  1. Ensure they're reachable from your machine.
  2. Set the environment variables:
export DTRACK_API_URL=https://dtrack.example.com
export DTRACK_API_KEY=<your-key>
export DEFECTDOJO_URL=https://defectdojo.example.com
export DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN=<your-token>
  1. Run the sync:
uv run ponvara sync

Or for GitHub:

export GITHUB_TOKEN=<your-token>
export GITHUB_ORG=my-org
uv run ponvara sync-github

⚠️ This will create/update products and findings in your DefectDojo instance. Use a dev or staging instance for testing.

docs.title: Code structure
docs.text:
• src/ponvara/__main__.py — CLI entry point and argument parsing
  • src/ponvara/config.py — environment variable loading (pydantic-settings)
  • src/ponvara/defectdojo.py — DefectDojo REST API client
  • src/ponvara/dependencytrack.py — Dependency-Track API client
  • src/ponvara/github.py — GitHub API client
  • src/ponvara/sync.py — core logic for Dependency-Track sync
  • src/ponvara/sync_github.py — core logic for GitHub Advanced Security sync
  • tests/ — test suite with mocked HTTP responses

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Follow the house conventions:

  • Branch naming: type/category/description (e.g., feat/sync/add-sonarqube-connector)
  • Commit messages: semantic-release format (feat(sync): add SonarQube connector)
  • Code style: Ruff formatting (run uv run ruff format before committing)
  • Type hints: Full type annotations on all functions
  • Tests: Every feature must have a passing test

See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full contributing guide.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: Ponvara's status is claimed here and nowhere else. If a maturity claim appears in another file in this repository, that file is wrong.

docs.title: Where it is now
docs.text: Phase 1: Dependency-Track and GitHub Advanced Security syncs to DefectDojo, ported off the Django ORM onto the DefectDojo REST API. Shipping as a Helm chart with two CronJobs (Dependency-Track sync and GitHub Advanced Security sync) plus ExternalSecrets.

docs.title: Implemented
docs.text:
Core sync engine:

  • Dependency-Track → DefectDojo via REST API (no Django ORM coupling)
  • GitHub Advanced Security → DefectDojo (code scanning, Dependabot, secret scanning)
  • Full test suite with mocked HTTP clients
  • Configuration via environment variables (pydantic-settings)
  • Helm chart with CronJob templates for both Dependency-Track and GitHub Advanced Security syncs

Next phases (TODO):

  • Phase 2: Zero-touch GitHub-issue push for High/Critical findings (tag-based dedup in DefectDojo)
  • Phase 3: Long-lived FastAPI + APScheduler service with /metrics, /sync/{source} endpoints
  • Phase 4: SonarQube connector and generalized source plugin architecture

docs.title: Phased migration
docs.text:
Low-risk and reversible; each phase leaves the previous one running until it's green. Full detail (risk + reversibility columns) in ../DESIGN.md.

Phase Change Status 0. Lift-and-shift New repo; move sync.py verbatim; add tests around the pure bits (target parsing, severity floor, issue body). Still the DefectDojo-image CronJob, still deployed from infra. ✅ DONE 1. Slim the image + GHAS Provision a ponvara DefectDojo API token (OCI Vault); replace the ORM token-mint with it; switch to python:3.12-slim. Add GitHub Advanced Security sync (code scanning, Dependabot, secret scanning). ✅ DONE 2. GitHub-issue push Implement zero-touch GitHub-issue push for High/Critical findings. Requires DefectDojo findings query and tag-based state tracking. Now fully version-decoupled. 📋 TODO 3. Long-lived service Convert to the FastAPI + APScheduler Deployment; add /metrics, /sync/{source}, ServiceMonitor; Helm chart; Flux app dir. Retire the infra CronJobs/ConfigMaps. 📋 TODO 4. Generalize Fold SonarQube in as a connector; document how a new source plugs in. Point future non-native sources here; leave native-parser tools pushing straight to DefectDojo. 📋 TODO

You can stop after Phase 1 or 2 and already have a tested, reviewable, slim, version-decoupled job — most of the value is there. Phases 3–4 deliver the long-lived backend and the reuse.

docs.title: Open decisions
docs.text:
Unresolved questions for future phases. Each should become an ADR with Status: Proposed once it has a shape.

Tracked in ../DESIGN.md § Open decisions:

  1. Tag-based dedup for GitHub push (Phase 2). Recommended: validate that reimport-scan preserves finding tags so GitHub-issue dedup can use them; fall back to finding hash if reimport recreates findings.
  2. Deployment vs CronJob-from-own-image (Phase 3) — "long-lived backend" points to Deployment; the chart supports both.
  3. Dedup state (Phase 2) — stateless via DefectDojo tags (recommended) vs a tiny service-owned Postgres (only if cross-source correlation/SLA is tracked here).
  4. Scope beyond Phase 1 — confirmed: Phase 2 adds GitHub-issue push; Phase 3 adds long-lived service; Phase 4 adds SonarQube connector and generalization.

docs.title: Via Helm chart (Kubernetes)
docs.text:
This is the recommended method for production deployments.

  1. Add the MagmaMoose Helm repository (if not already added):
helm repo add magmamoose https://magmamoose.github.io/helm-charts
helm repo update
  1. Provision the required OCI Vault secrets (see Prerequisites):
  2. dependency-track-api-key

  3. ponvara-dd-token

  4. Install the chart:

helm install ponvara magmamoose/ponvara \
  --namespace security \
  --create-namespace \
  --set defectDojo.url=https://defectdojo.magmamoose.com \
  --set dependencyTrack.url=https://dtrack.magmamoose.com
  1. Verify the CronJob is created:
kubectl get cronjob -n security
kubectl describe cronjob ponvara -n security

docs.title: Enabling GitHub Advanced Security sync
docs.text:
To enable the GitHub Advanced Security sync, add the second CronJob:

helm install ponvara ... \
  --set github.enabled=true \
  --set github.org=my-org

Or edit the values file:

github:
  enabled: true
  org: my-org  # or set github.repos: "owner/repo,owner/repo2"

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
For development or testing locally:

  1. Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/MagmaMoose/ponvara
cd ponvara
  1. Install dependencies:
pip install -e .

Or using uv:

uv sync
  1. Set environment variables:
export DTRACK_API_URL=https://dtrack.example.com
export DTRACK_API_KEY=<your-key>
export DEFECTDOJO_URL=https://defectdojo.example.com
export DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN=<your-token>
  1. Run a sync:
ponvara sync

docs.title: Via Docker image
docs.text:
The image is published to ghcr.io/magmamoose/ponvara:latest.

docker run \
  -e DTRACK_API_URL=https://dtrack.example.com \
  -e DTRACK_API_KEY=<your-key> \
  -e DEFECTDOJO_URL=https://defectdojo.example.com \
  -e DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN=<your-token> \
  ghcr.io/magmamoose/ponvara:latest \
  ponvara sync

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After installation, verify the setup by checking:

  1. The CronJob runs successfully:
kubectl logs -n security -l app=ponvara --tail=50

  1. Findings appear in DefectDojo in the reimported products.

  2. No error messages about missing credentials in the logs.

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or later (for running from source; the container image uses Python 3.12-slim)
  • Kubernetes 1.19+ (for Helm chart deployment)

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
• Dependency-Track 4.8+ — for ponvara sync
  • DefectDojo 2.16+ — required for all sync operations
  • GitHub (cloud or self-hosted) — for ponvara sync-github

docs.title: Credentials and provisioning
docs.text: Before running Ponvara, provision the required credentials:

docs.title: Dependency-Track
docs.text: • A Dependency-Track API key with read access to all projects you want to sync.

docs.title: DefectDojo
docs.text:
• A provisioned DefectDojo API token for a service user account. This must be created manually in DefectDojo (User Management → Add User → set as API user, then copy the token). Ponvara does not mint tokens.
  • The service user must have permission to create products and findings.

docs.title: GitHub (optional, only for ponvara sync-github)
docs.text:
• A GitHub personal access token (or fine-grained token) with read access to code scanning alerts, Dependabot alerts, and secret scanning alerts for the repositories you want to sync.
  • For GitHub Enterprise, you'll also need to set GITHUB_API_URL to your GHE instance.

docs.title: In Kubernetes
docs.text:
When deploying via Helm chart:

  • ExternalSecrets Operator must be installed and configured with a ClusterSecretStore pointing to OCI Vault (or another secret store).
  • Vault keys must be provisioned before the chart is deployed:
  • dependency-track-api-key — the Dependency-Track API key
  • ponvara-dd-token — the DefectDojo service-user API token
  • ponvara-github-token — the GitHub token (only required if github.enabled=true)

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
• Ponvara must reach Dependency-Track, DefectDojo, and (optionally) GitHub APIs.
  • In-cluster defaults use Kubernetes service DNS; adjust if services are in different namespaces.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Get a Dependency-Track to DefectDojo sync running in 5 minutes.

docs.title: What you'll need
docs.text:
• A running Dependency-Track instance with at least one project
  • A running DefectDojo instance with an API token for a service user
  • A Kubernetes cluster with the Helm chart installed (or Python 3.11+ for running locally)

docs.title: Step 1: Provision the DefectDojo token
docs.text:
If you don't already have one, create a new service-user API token in DefectDojo:

  1. Go to DefectDojo Admin → Users.
  2. Click Add User.
  3. Set the username to ponvara and mark it as an API user.
  4. Copy the token that DefectDojo generates.
  5. Store it in OCI Vault under the key ponvara-dd-token.

docs.title: Step 2: Install via Helm
docs.text:
helm repo add magmamoose https://magmamoose.github.io/helm-charts
helm repo update

helm install ponvara magmamoose/ponvara \
  --namespace security \
  --create-namespace \
  --set defectDojo.url=https://defectdojo.example.com \
  --set dependencyTrack.url=https://dtrack.example.com

The chart assumes your OCI Vault keys are provisioned. If they're not, the pods will fail to start with a vault error.

docs.title: Step 3: Verify
docs.text:
Wait a moment for the CronJob to schedule, then check the logs:

kubectl logs -n security -l app=ponvara --tail=50

You should see lines like:

ponvara: syncing Dependency-Track projects to DefectDojo
ponvara: project_1: created product in DefectDojo
ponvara: done

Then check DefectDojo: a new product should have appeared for each Dependency-Track project, with findings reimported.

docs.title: (Optional) Enable GitHub Advanced Security sync
docs.text:
Add the second CronJob:

helm upgrade ponvara magmamoose/ponvara \
  --set github.enabled=true \
  --set github.org=my-org

Ponvara will now run sync-github every 6 hours (or set github.schedule to change the cron expression).

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
• The Dependency-Track sync runs hourly. Each run reimports the latest findings from Dependency-Track.
  • The GitHub sync (if enabled) runs every 6 hours and reimports code scanning, Dependabot, and secret scanning alerts.
  • Findings are deduplicated by DefectDojo's reimport-scan endpoint, so re-runs don't create duplicates.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Pod fails to start: - Check that your OCI Vault keys (dependency-track-api-key, ponvara-dd-token) are provisioned. - Run kubectl describe pod -n security and look for vault-related errors.

No findings appear in DefectDojo: - Check that Dependency-Track has projects with findings. - Check the pod logs: kubectl logs -n security -l app=ponvara. - Verify the DefectDojo service is reachable from the cluster: kubectl run --rm -it --image=curlimages/curl -l app=test -- curl http://defectdojo-django.security.svc.cluster.local/health/.

Wrong URL or token: - Edit the Helm values and re-run helm upgrade ponvara magmamoose/ponvara --set ....

For more, see Configuration and CLI reference.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: Ponvara runs as one-shot commands scheduled by a CronJob. Each command reads configuration from environment variables, syncs findings once, and exits.

docs.title: ponvara sync
docs.text:
Syncs Dependency-Track projects into DefectDojo via the REST API.

ponvara sync

Requires DTRACK_API_KEY and DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN. Reads every project from Dependency-Track, exports its findings as FPF, and reimports them into DefectDojo under a product named after the project.

Exit codes: - 0 — success or skipped projects (partial failures are logged, not fatal) - 1 — setup/fatal error (missing token, network unreachable)

docs.title: ponvara sync-github
docs.text:
Syncs GitHub Advanced Security findings into DefectDojo.

ponvara sync-github

Requires GITHUB_TOKEN and DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN. Must also set either GITHUB_REPOS (explicit list) or GITHUB_ORG (enumerate all repositories). Reads code scanning (SARIF), Dependabot, and secret scanning from each repository and reimports into DefectDojo.

Exit codes: - 0 — success or skipped repositories - 1 — setup/fatal error (missing token, no repos configured)

docs.title: Global options
docs.text:
ponvara --version

Prints the version and exits.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success (all or partial runs; per-source failures are logged) 1 Setup or fatal network error (missing token, source unreachable)

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Both commands log to stderr with the prefix ponvara: at INFO level by default. Run via docker run or kubectl logs to capture output.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Ponvara reads configuration from environment variables. In Kubernetes, these come from an ExternalSecret that pulls from OCI Vault.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Type Default Required Description DTRACK_API_URL string http://dependency-track-api-server.security.svc.cluster.local:8080 no Dependency-Track API base URL. Defaults to in-cluster service. DTRACK_API_KEY string (empty) yes Dependency-Track API key. Required for ponvara sync. DEFECTDOJO_URL string http://defectdojo-django.security.svc.cluster.local no DefectDojo base URL. Defaults to in-cluster service. DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN string (empty) yes DefectDojo API token. Required for ponvara sync and ponvara sync-github. Must be provisioned in advance (not minted at runtime). DD_PRODUCT_TYPE string Dependency-Track no DefectDojo product type for Dependency-Track findings. DD_ENGAGEMENT string Dependency Track no DefectDojo engagement name for Dependency-Track findings. DD_SITE_URL string https://defectdojo.magmamoose.com no The site URL for DefectDojo (used in finding context). GITHUB_API_URL string https://api.github.com no GitHub API base URL. Use for self-hosted GitHub Enterprise. GITHUB_TOKEN string (empty) yes (if using sync-github) GitHub personal access token. Required for ponvara sync-github. GITHUB_REPOS string (empty) no Explicit comma-separated list of repositories (e.g., owner/repo,owner/repo2). Takes precedence over GITHUB_ORG. GITHUB_ORG string (empty) no GitHub organization to enumerate all repositories from. Used only if GITHUB_REPOS is empty. At least one of these must be set for ponvara sync-github. DD_GITHUB_PRODUCT_TYPE string GitHub Advanced Security no DefectDojo product type for GitHub findings. DD_GITHUB_ENGAGEMENT string GHAS no DefectDojo engagement name for GitHub findings. HTTP_TIMEOUT float 300.0 no HTTP request timeout in seconds. VERIFY_SSL boolean true no Whether to verify SSL certificates. Set to false for self-signed certificates.

docs.title: Loading precedence
docs.text: Configuration is loaded from .env file first (if present), then environment variables override it. Case is insensitive; extra variables are ignored.

docs.title: Helm defaults
docs.text:
The Ponvara Helm chart sets defaults for the CronJob. See the values.yaml in the repository for the complete configuration, including:

  • CronJob schedule (hourly for Dependency-Track, every 6 hours for GitHub)
  • Resource requests and limits (50m CPU, 128Mi memory)
  • Security context (non-root, no privilege escalation, read-only filesystem)
  • ExternalSecret references to OCI Vault

docs.title: Secrets handling
docs.text: All secret values (DTRACK_API_KEY, DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN) are sourced from OCI Vault via ExternalSecrets Operator. The defectDojo token must be provisioned in advance as a DefectDojo service user — Ponvara does not mint tokens.

docs.title: Example: Docker
docs.text:
docker run -e DTRACK_API_URL=https://dtrack.example.com \
  -e DTRACK_API_KEY=<your-key> \
  -e DEFECTDOJO_URL=https://defectdojo.example.com \
  -e DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN=<your-token> \
  ghcr.io/magmamoose/ponvara:0.1.0 \
  ponvara sync

docs.title: Example: Kubernetes (via Helm)
docs.text:
The Helm chart configures ExternalSecrets to pull secrets from OCI Vault:

helm install ponvara charts/ponvara \
  --set defectDojo.url=https://defectdojo.example.com \
  --set dependencyTrack.url=https://dtrack.example.com

The chart's ExternalSecret references read dependency-track-api-key and ponvara-dd-token from OCI Vault.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Ponvara is deployed as Kubernetes CronJobs via a Helm chart. Phase 1 runs two scheduled one-shot commands; future phases will add a long-lived FastAPI service.

docs.title: Helm chart overview
docs.text:
The chart creates:

  • CronJob for ponvara sync (Dependency-Track → DefectDojo), scheduled hourly.
  • CronJob for ponvara sync-github (GitHub Advanced Security → DefectDojo), scheduled every 6 hours (optional, disabled by default).
  • ExternalSecret to materialize API keys from OCI Vault into environment variables.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Key Helm values:

image:
  repository: ghcr.io/magmamoose/ponvara
  tag: "" # defaults to Chart.appVersion
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent

schedule: "0 * * * *" # hourly for Dependency-Track sync

concurrencyPolicy: Forbid # only one pod at a time
backoffLimit: 1 # don't retry failed pods
activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800 # kill pods that run longer than 30 minutes

dependencyTrack:
  url: http://dependency-track-api-server.security.svc.cluster.local:8080

defectDojo:
  url: http://defectdojo-django.security.svc.cluster.local
  productType: "Dependency-Track"
  engagement: "Dependency Track"

github:
  enabled: false
  schedule: "0 */6 * * *" # every 6 hours

# Resource limits (house convention: request CPU, limit memory only)
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 50m
    memory: 128Mi
  limits:
    memory: 256Mi

# Security hardening
podSecurityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 10001
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault
securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  capabilities:
    drop: ["ALL"]

See the full values.yaml for all options.

docs.title: Secrets handling
docs.text:
The chart uses ExternalSecrets Operator to pull secrets from OCI Vault:

externalSecrets:
  enabled: true
  store: oci-vault
  storeKind: ClusterSecretStore
  dtrackApiKeyRef: dependency-track-api-key
  defectDojoTokenRef: ponvara-dd-token
  githubTokenRef: ponvara-github-token # only when github.enabled=true

Each *Ref is the key name in OCI Vault. The values are materialized into environment variables that the pods read.

docs.title: Dependency-Track sync
docs.text:
• Default: Every hour at :00 (0 * * * *)
  • Why: Reimport scan dedupes findings, so hourly is safe. Original legacy job was hourly.

docs.title: GitHub Advanced Security sync
docs.text:
• Default: Every 6 hours (0 */6 * * *)
  • Why: GitHub advanced security doesn't change as rapidly; 6 hours reduces API quota pressure.

Both are configurable via schedule (Dependency-Track) and github.schedule (GitHub) in values.yaml.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
If a sync pod crashes or gets stuck:

  1. Check the pod logs:
kubectl logs -n security <pod-name>

  1. The pod will not be retried (backoffLimit: 1), but the next scheduled run will proceed.

  2. If you need to force an immediate manual sync, run the image as a one-shot:

kubectl run -it --rm \
  -e DTRACK_API_KEY=$DTRACK_API_KEY \
  -e DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN=$DEFECTDOJO_TOKEN \
  --image=ghcr.io/magmamoose/ponvara:0.1.0 \
  ponvara-manual \
  -- ponvara sync

docs.title: Monitoring and observability
docs.text:
Phase 1 has no built-in metrics. Future phases (Phase 3+) will add:

  • Prometheus metrics (/metrics endpoint)
  • ServiceMonitor for integration with Prometheus
  • Health checks (/health)

For now, monitoring is via pod logs and DefectDojo's audit trail.

docs.title: Upgrading the chart
docs.text:
To upgrade Ponvara to a new version:

helm repo update magmamoose
helm upgrade ponvara magmamoose/ponvara --namespace security

The next scheduled run will pick up the new image. No downtime (pods are stateless).

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text:
helm uninstall ponvara --namespace security

This removes the CronJobs and ExternalSecret. Findings already in DefectDojo are not deleted.
